draft.title: Horizontal translations
card: The graph of y = f(x + b) is the graph of y = f(x) moved sideways by b units. The shape does not change, and only the position does.
The shift goes the opposite way to the sign. y = f(x + b) with b positive moves the graph left by b. y = f(x − b) moves it right by b.
Why: in y = f(x + 3), the input x + 3 reaches the old value of x when x is 3 less. So each point appears 3 units further left.
Example: y = x² has its vertex at (0, 0). For y = (x − 5)², the vertex is at (5, 0), so the graph has moved 5 units right.
draft.remember: Inside the brackets, the shift is the opposite of the sign: +b moves left, −b moves right.

a.q: The graph of y = f(x) is moved 4 units to the left. What is the equation of the new graph?
a.why: A move of 4 units left is written f(x + 4), because the shift is opposite to the sign. f(x − 4) is the tempting choice, but it moves the graph right. The options with +4 or −4 outside the brackets move the graph up or down.
a.clue: The sideways shift goes inside the brackets, and its sign is opposite to the direction.

b.q: The graph of y = x² has its vertex at (0, 0). Where is the vertex of y = (x + 2)²?
b.why: y = (x + 2)² is y = x² moved 2 units left, so the vertex goes from (0, 0) to (−2, 0). (2, 0) is the tempting wrong answer, as it follows the sign instead of reversing it. The points with x = 0 would come from adding or subtracting outside the brackets.
b.clue: Find the x value that makes the bracket equal 0.
